text: He's nineteen, and he's just done something no footballer had ever done.
Lamine Yamal has won the Kopa Trophy for the third year in a row: the award for the best young player in the world.
Before him, Em-bappay, Pedri, Gavi and Bellingham each won it once. Nobody had ever won it three times.
At the twenty twenty-six Ballon Dor in London, he finished third, behind Harry Kane and Kylian Em-bappay. A year earlier, he was second.
His father is from Morocco, his mother from Equatorial Guinea, and he grew up in Rocafonda, in Mataro. That's his three-zero-four celebration: the end of the neighbourhood's postcode.
He joined La Maseea, Barsa's academy, in twenty fourteen, when he was still a little kid.
He made his first-team debut at just fifteen years, nine months and sixteen days old.
With Spain, he won Euro twenty twenty-four and the twenty twenty-six World Cup: the youngest player ever to win both.
Now he wears Barsa's number ten, the shirt that once belonged to Messi.
Joan Laporta says he's convinced Lamine will win the Ballon Dor one day. Do you agree? Tell us in the comments.
